scenes.tts: Two kinds of sensory axon enter the spinal cord side by side. One kind stops in the dorsal horn. The other runs on to the motor neurons. What sorts them?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Cue Marks the Place. Spinal cord cross-section. A thin red axon and a thick blue axon enter together at the dorsal root entry zone. Red stops in the dorsal horn; blue runs on to motor neurons in the ventral horn. Question on screen: what sorts them?
scenes.narration: Two kinds of sensory axon enter the spinal cord side by side. One kind stops in the dorsal horn. The other runs on to the motor neurons. What sorts them?

scenes.tts: The ones that stop are small pain and temperature fibres. They depend on nerve growth factor. The ones that go on are large muscle stretch fibres. They depend on neurotrophin three.
scenes.caption: The ones that stop are small pain and temperature fibres. They depend on nerve growth factor (NGF). The ones that go on are large muscle stretch fibres. They depend on neurotrophin-3 (NT-3).
scenes.visual: Two neurons in a dorsal root ganglion. Red, small: labels pain and temperature, NGF, TrkA. Blue, large: labels muscle stretch, NT-3, TrkC.
scenes.narration: The ones that stop are small pain and temperature fibres. They depend on nerve growth factor (NGF). The ones that go on are large muscle stretch fibres. They depend on neurotrophin-3 (NT-3).

scenes.tts: The ventral cord was known to release something that inhibits sensory axon growth. A map needs walls as well as roads.
scenes.visual: The ventral half of the cross-section shades in a warning colour. Label: ventral cord releases an inhibitor of sensory axon growth.
scenes.narration: The ventral cord was known to release something that inhibits sensory axon growth. A map needs walls as well as roads.

scenes.tts: To find a wall, you need an assay. Raper and Kapfhammer grew chick sensory neurons in a dish. Then they added membranes from embryonic brain.
scenes.visual: A culture dish. Chick dorsal root ganglion neurons on laminin, each axon ending in a spread growth cone. A suspension of brain membranes is added. Label: Raper and Kapfhammer, 1990.
scenes.narration: To find a wall, you need an assay. Raper and Kapfhammer grew chick sensory neurons in a dish. Then they added membranes from embryonic brain.

scenes.tts: Within minutes, many of the spread growth cones folded into thin tips. That is collapse. The fraction that collapsed was the readout. Remove the membranes, and the effect reverses.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse style: a field of broad growth cone fans with filopodia; most fold into thin tips, a few stay spread. Label: collapse, within minutes; count the fraction collapsed. Membranes washed out; the fans spread again. Label: reversible.
scenes.narration: Within minutes, many of the spread growth cones folded into thin tips. That is collapse. The fraction that collapsed was the readout. Remove the membranes, and the effect reverses.

scenes.tts: Would any membrane do this? And what kind of molecule is doing it?
scenes.visual: Two question marks over the dish: any membrane? what molecule?
scenes.narration: Would any membrane do this? And what kind of molecule is doing it?

scenes.tts: Membranes from liver or fibroblasts did not cause collapse. So not just any membrane would do. Heat and trypsin destroyed the activity. So it was a protein.
scenes.visual: Three small dishes: liver membranes, growth cone stays spread; fibroblast membranes, stays spread; heated or trypsin-treated brain membranes, stays spread. Label: a protein.
scenes.narration: Membranes from liver or fibroblasts did not cause collapse. So not just any membrane would do. Heat and trypsin destroyed the activity. So it was a protein.

scenes.tts: Raper's group purified it from chick brain and named it collapsin. Today it is called Sema three A, a semaphorin.
scenes.caption: Raper's group purified it from chick brain and named it collapsin. Today it is called Sema3A, a semaphorin.
scenes.visual: A purified protein drawn as a single glyph. Labels: collapsin, about 100 kilodaltons, Luo, Raible and Raper, 1993. The label morphs to Sema3A.
scenes.narration: Raper's group purified it from chick brain and named it collapsin. Today it is called Sema3A, a semaphorin.

scenes.tts: Then came a first clue. Growth cones from the retina did not respond to it.
scenes.visual: A retinal growth cone bathed in collapsin stays fully spread beside a collapsed sensory growth cone.
scenes.narration: Then came a first clue. Growth cones from the retina did not respond to it.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry through. The cue marks the place. The growth cone decides what it means.
scenes.visual: Rule on screen: The cue marks the place; the growth cone decides what it means.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry through. The cue marks the place. The growth cone decides what it means.

scenes.tts: Does a growth cone answer the cue at all? First, it needs the receptor.
scenes.visual: Rule card with three rows appearing. Row 1: answers at all? needs the receptor.
scenes.narration: Does a growth cone answer the cue at all? First, it needs the receptor.

scenes.tts: Which way does it answer? That depends on its internal state.
scenes.visual: Row 2: which way? depends on internal state, such as cyclic GMP.
scenes.narration: Which way does it answer? That depends on its internal state.

scenes.tts: If it is repelled, does it turn, or collapse? In typical assays, a gradient from one side turns it away. A high dose all round can fold it up, where the preparation supports collapse. Layout, dose, exposure and the cell all matter.
scenes.visual: Row 3: if repelled, turn or collapse? Typical outcomes under assay conditions. Small growth cone icons: gradient from one side, turning away; strong cue all round, possible collapse. Label: layout, dose, exposure, cell state.
scenes.narration: If it is repelled, does it turn, or collapse? In typical assays, a gradient from one side turns it away. A high dose all round can fold it up, where the preparation supports collapse. Layout, dose, exposure and the cell all matter.

scenes.tts: The rule has limits. Which cue is made, where, and how much still matter. And in the living cord, other cues share the job.
scenes.visual: Small caption under the rule card: limits. The cue still carries information; other cues share the work in the cord.
scenes.narration: The rule has limits. Which cue is made, where, and how much still matter. And in the living cord, other cues share the job.

scenes.tts: Back to the two axons. One wall, two answers. The takeaway: the same cue stops one axon, and barely affects the other.
scenes.visual: Return to the cross-section: red axon halts at the shaded ventral cord, blue axon passes through. Takeaway on screen: same cue, two answers.
scenes.narration: Back to the two axons. One wall, two answers. The takeaway: the same cue stops one axon, and barely affects the other.
